1.note: Here Qoheleth uses or invents a proverb in order to teach that what people remember about a person is worth more than what money can buy. Translate this proverb in a way that will be recognized as a proverb and be meaningful in your language and culture. Alternate translation: [A good name is better than fine perfume]
Here, **name** represents a person’s reputation. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [a good reputation]

The implication is that **good oil** is expensive perfumed oil, which people in this culture valued highly. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [than costly perfumed oil]

Qoheleth is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [and better is the day of death than the day of his being born]

The expression **his being born** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [than the day when his mother bore him]

2.note: Here, **a house of mourning** and **a house of a banquet** represent the gatherings that people hold in those places. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [a funeral than to go to a feast]

Qoheleth is referring to dying in a polite way by using the phrase **the end of all humanity**. Depending on what is helpful for your readers, you could use a polite way of referring to this in your language, or you could state this plainly. Alternate translation: [death is what awaits all humanity]

Qoheleth is using **will give {it} to his heart** as a common expression of the culture to mean “will think carefully about it.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and the living should reflect seriously on that]

Qoheleth is using the adjective **the living** as a noun to mean a certain kind of person. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [and a person who is alive]

3.note: If your language does not use abstract nouns for the ideas of **grief** and **laughter**, you could express the same ideas in another way. Alternate translation: [Better to grieve than to laugh]

Qoheleth is using **a bad face** as a common expression of the culture to mean “a sad expression.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [with a sad expression]

Here Qoheleth is speaking as if a person’s inner self were his **heart**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [a person may be well within himself]

4.note: Here Qoheleth is speaking as if the thoughts and inclinations of wise people were their **heart**, which could be in a place. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Wise people set their minds on a house of mourning]

5.note: Qoheleth is not referring to a specific **person**. He means people in general. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [than for someone to listen to a song of fools]

The implication is that **a song of fools** is entertainment and flattery that pleases a person but teaches him nothing. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [the pleasant but empty singing of fools]

6.q: כְ⁠ק֤וֹל הַ⁠סִּירִים֙ תַּ֣חַת הַ⁠סִּ֔יר כֵּ֖ן שְׂחֹ֣ק הַ⁠כְּסִ֑יל
6.note: The point of this comparison is that just as **the sound of the thorns under the cooking-pot** is loud but produces almost no heat, so is **the laughter of the fool** loud but worth nothing. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [just as thorns crackle loudly under the cooking-pot but give almost no heat, so the laughter of the fool is loud but accomplishes nothing]

Qoheleth is using words with similar sounds for poetic effect. In the original language, the word for **the thorns** sounds almost the same as the word for **the cooking-pot**. You may want to reproduce this effect if poetry in your language does this.
See how you translated the similar expression in 6:2. Alternate translation: [And this also is like a passing breath]

7.q: כִּ֥י הָ⁠עֹ֖שֶׁק יְהוֹלֵ֣ל חָכָ֑ם וִֽ⁠יאַבֵּ֥ד אֶת־לֵ֖ב מַתָּנָֽה
7.note: These two clauses mean basically the same thing. The second emphasizes the meaning of the first by repeating the same idea with different words. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could combine them and express the emphasis in another way. Alternate translation: [Surely corrupt gain completely ruins the mind of even a wise person]

Qoheleth is speaking of **oppression** as if it were a living thing that could drive a person out of his mind. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [a wise person loses his mind when others oppress him]

Here Qoheleth is speaking as if a person’s ability to judge rightly were his **heart**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and a bribe destroys a person’s ability to judge rightly]

8.note: Qoheleth is using **length of spirit** as a common expression of the culture to mean “patience.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [is patience]

Qoheleth is using **height of spirit** as a common expression of the culture to mean “pride.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [than pride]

9.note: Qoheleth is using **hasten in your spirit to become angry** as a common expression of the culture to mean “become angry quickly.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Do not become angry quickly]

Qoheleth is speaking of **anger** as if it were a living thing that could settle down and rest in a person’s **lap**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [fools are characterized by anger]

10.q: מֶ֣ה הָיָ֔ה שֶׁ֤⁠הַ⁠יָּמִים֙ הָ⁠רִ֣אשֹׁנִ֔ים הָי֥וּ טוֹבִ֖ים מֵ⁠אֵ֑לֶּה
10.note: Qoheleth is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [What was the reason that the former days were better than these days]

11.note: The implication is that **Wisdom** brings the kind of benefit that wealth brings. This could mean that wisdom is (1) as good as an inheritance or (2) good along with an inheritance. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [Wisdom is as valuable as an inheritance]

If your language does not use abstract nouns for the ideas of **Wisdom** and **an inheritance**, you could express the same ideas in another way. Alternate translation: [To be wise is good along with what a person inherits]

Qoheleth is using **those who see the sun** as a common expression of the culture to mean “people who are alive.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [to those who are living]

12.note: Here Qoheleth is speaking as if the protection that wisdom and money give a person were **the shadow** that they cast. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [as wisdom gives protection, so also does silver give protection]
Here, **silver** represents money and possessions in general. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [riches]

Qoheleth is using the possessive form to describe **an advantage** that **knowledge** gives a person. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [And this is an advantage that knowledge gives a person]

Qoheleth is speaking of **Wisdom** as if it were a living thing that could keep alive the people who have it. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Being wise keeps people alive]

13.note: Here Qoheleth is speaking as if the way that God orders events were something that God had **bent** and no one could **straighten**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [to change what he has determined]

14.q: בְּ⁠י֤וֹם טוֹבָה֙ הֱיֵ֣ה בְ⁠ט֔וֹב וּ⁠בְ⁠י֥וֹם רָעָ֖ה רְאֵ֑ה
14.note: Qoheleth is referring to all of the circumstances of a person’s life by naming two extremes, **a day of good** and **a day of misfortune**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [In whatever circumstances you find yourself, consider this]

Qoheleth is using **be in good** as a common expression of the culture to mean “enjoy what is good.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [enjoy the good things]

The first occurrence of the pronoun **this** refers to **a day of good**, while the second refers to **a day of misfortune**. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [the God has made the day of good as well as the day of misfortune]

Qoheleth is using **cannot find anything after him** as a common expression of the culture to mean “cannot discover what God has planned.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [humanity cannot discover what God has planned]

15.note: Here Qoheleth is speaking as if his lifetime were **vapor**, which appears for a moment and then is gone. See how you translated the similar expression in 1:14. Alternate translation: [in the days of my brief life]

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **his righteousness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [perishing even though he acts righteously]

Qoheleth is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [lengthening his days in his evil]

16.note: The implication is that Qoheleth is warning against a kind of excess, not against being righteous. This could mean: (1) being self-righteous. Alternate translation: [Do not be self-righteous] or (2) being excessively scrupulous about doing what is right. Alternate translation: [Do not be excessively scrupulous].

The expression **be shocked** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [why should life shock you]

17.note: Qoheleth is using the question form to warn his readers about the consequence of being wicked and foolish. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [otherwise you will die before your time has come!]

Qoheleth is using **not your time** as a common expression of the culture to mean “before the time when you would otherwise die.” This could mean: (1) that the person dies needlessly young because of their own foolishness. Alternate translation: [sooner than you need to] or (2) that God cuts their life short. Alternate translation: [because God is displeased with your wickedness]

18.note: The first occurrence of the pronoun **this** refers to the warning against being overly righteous and wise, while the second refers to the warning against being wicked and foolish. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [you should take hold of this warning against being overly righteous and wise, and also from that warning against being wicked and foolish]

Here Qoheleth is speaking as if his advice were an object that a person could **take hold of**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [you should pay attention to this advice]

Qoheleth is using **do not let your hand rest** as a common expression of the culture to mean “do not let go of it.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [do not loosen your grip]

Qoheleth is using **will go forth with both of them** as a common expression of the culture to mean “will come safely through both of these.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [will come safely through both of these dangers]

19.q: הַֽ⁠חָכְמָ֖ה תָּעֹ֣ז לֶ⁠חָכָ֑ם מֵֽ⁠עֲשָׂרָה֙ שַׁלִּיטִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר הָי֖וּ בָּ⁠עִֽיר
19.note: Here Qoheleth is speaking as if wisdom were a defense that makes a person **strong**, the way that **rulers** defend a city. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Wisdom protects the wise person better than ten rulers can protect the city]

Qoheleth is using the adjective **the wise** as a noun to mean a certain kind of person. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [for a wise person]

Qoheleth says **ten rulers** as an extreme statement for emphasis. He means a large number of powerful officials. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use a different way to express the emphasis. Alternate translation: [more than a whole group of powerful rulers in the city]

20.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you may want to put the information about **a person** with the information about there not being **a righteous {person} on the earth**. Alternate translation: [For there is not a righteous person among the people on the earth]

20.q: אֵ֥ין צַדִּ֖יק בָּ⁠אָ֑רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֥ר יַעֲשֶׂה־טּ֖וֹב וְ⁠לֹ֥א יֶחֱטָֽא
20.note: Here Qoheleth uses or invents a proverb in order to state that every person sins. Translate this proverb in a way that will be recognized as a proverb and be meaningful in your language and culture. Alternate translation: [no righteous man walks the earth who does only good and never sins]

21.q: לְ⁠כָל הַ⁠דְּבָרִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יְדַבֵּ֔רוּ אַל תִּתֵּ֖ן לִבֶּ֑⁠ךָ
21.note: If it would be helpful in your language, you could change the order of these phrases. Alternate translation: [do not give your heart to all of the words that they say]

Qoheleth is using the pronoun **they** in a general sense, not to refer to specific people. Use an expression for this that would be natural in your language. Alternate translation: [that anyone says]

Qoheleth is using **do not give your heart** as a common expression of the culture to mean “do not pay attention.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [do not listen to them]

The implication is that it would be especially painful to hear **your servant** speak badly of you, since a servant owed his master respect. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [even your own servant, who owes you respect, speaking badly of you]

22.note: Qoheleth is using **your heart knows** as a common expression of the culture to mean “you yourself are aware.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [you know]

Qoheleth is stating the pronoun **you** separately, even though the verb translated as **have belittled** already includes this meaning. He is doing that to emphasize that his readers have done the very thing that they would not want to hear. If a speaker of your language would use an explicit pronoun for the same purpose, you may want to use that construction in your translation. If not, your language may have other ways of showing the meaning here. Alternate translation: [even you yourself have belittled others]

Qoheleth is using the adjective **others** as a noun to mean a certain kind of person. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [other people]

23.note: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **wisdom**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [by thinking wisely]
If it would be more natural in your language, you could express this as an indirect quotation. Alternate translation: [I said that I would be wise,]

Qoheleth is using **far from me** as a common expression of the culture to mean “beyond my ability to understand.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [was beyond what I could understand]

24.note: Here Qoheleth is speaking as if what he wanted to understand were **Far away** and **deep** in a place that he could not reach. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Beyond understanding is that which was. And profoundly mysterious]

Qoheleth is repeating forms of the word **deep** in order to intensify his expression of the idea that it conveys. If your language can repeat words for intensification, it would be appropriate to do that here in your translation. If not, your language may have another way of expressing the intensification. Alternate translation: [And extremely deep]

Qoheleth is using the question form to emphasize that no one is able to understand these things. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [no one can find it.]

25.note: Qoheleth is speaking of his **heart** as if it were a living thing that could search alongside him. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I turned with all my mind]

Qoheleth is stating the pronoun **I** separately, even though the verb translated as **I turned** already includes this meaning. He is doing that to emphasize that he himself gave his whole attention to this search. If a speaker of your language would use an explicit pronoun for the same purpose, you may want to use that construction in your translation. If not, your language may have other ways of showing the meaning here. Alternate translation: [I myself turned my whole heart]

The terms **to know**, **to explore**, and **{to} seek** mean similar things. Qoheleth is using the three terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [to diligently search out]

The terms **{the} wickedness {that is} folly** and **the foolishness {that is} madness** mean similar things. Qoheleth is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [how completely senseless wicked madness is]

26.note: Here Qoheleth is speaking as if the distress that this woman causes were a taste that was **more bitter than death**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [more painful to endure than dying]

Qoheleth is stating the pronoun **she** separately, even though the phrase **the woman who** already indicates whom he is talking about. He is doing that to emphasize what this woman is like. If a speaker of your language would use an explicit pronoun for the same purpose, you may want to use that construction in your translation. If not, your language may have other ways of showing the meaning here. Alternate translation: [the woman who is truly nothing but snares]

The implication is that Qoheleth is describing something that traps a man and ruins him. This could mean: (1) a seductive woman. Alternate translation: [the seductive woman, and she is] or (2) folly, which Qoheleth pictures as a woman. Alternate translation: [the folly, and it is] You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers.

Qoheleth is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [and her heart is a net, and her hands are chains]

Here Qoheleth is speaking as if this woman’s intentions were **nets** for catching a man. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and her heart, intent on catching men]

Here Qoheleth is speaking as if this woman’s hold on a man were **chains**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [her hands hold a man tightly so that he cannot escape]
See how you translated the similar expression in 2:26.

The expression **will be captured** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [but she will capture a sinner]

27.note: The phrase **says Qoheleth** introduces a direct quotation. In your translation, use a natural way of indicating direct quotations in your language.

Qoheleth is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [I examined one thing after another in order to find the scheme of things]
See how you translated this name in [1:1](ta:01).

28.note: Qoheleth is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [while still my soul sought the scheme of things, but I have not found it]
Here, **my soul** represents the seeker himself. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [I kept searching]

28.q: אָדָ֞ם אֶחָ֤ד מֵ⁠אֶ֨לֶף֙ מָצָ֔אתִי וְ⁠אִשָּׁ֥ה בְ⁠כָל אֵ֖לֶּה לֹ֥א מָצָֽאתִי
28.note: If it would be helpful in your language, you could change the order of these clauses. Alternate translation: [Among a thousand people, I found one man, but among all of these people, I did not find the woman]

Qoheleth says **a thousand {men}** as an extreme statement for emphasis. He means a very large number of people. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use a different way to express the emphasis. Alternate translation: [One man from a very great number of men]

29.note: Here Qoheleth is speaking as if living rightly were standing **upright**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [God made people to live rightly]

Qoheleth is stating the pronoun **they** along with the verb translated as **have sought out**, which already includes its meaning. He is doing that because he is contrasting what God did with what **humanity** has done. If a speaker of your language would use an explicit pronoun for the same purpose, you may want to use that construction in your translation. If not, your language may have other ways of showing that meaning here. Alternate translation: [but they have sought out many schemes]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **schemes**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [how they might scheme in many ways]
